IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248#2/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248#2/r7.claim: أمة means religion in the phrase about the fathers' way; al-Nābigha's ذو أمة means a person of religion, and the word originally named people united in one religion.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248#2/r7.anchor: والأمة: الدين، قال تعالى: إنا وجدنا آباءنا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r2.claim: Appealing to forefathers does not establish idolatry; the idolaters need evidence from revelation, reason, or human nature, or they face the fate of earlier deniers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r2.anchor: The only argument they have to associate the angels in Godhead is that their forefathers regarded this to be so

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p366/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p366/r12.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p366/r12.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, Abū Sufyān, Abū Jahl, ʿUtba, and Shayba ibn Rabīʿa of Quraysh, consoling the Messenger by comparison with earlier deniers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p366/r12.anchor: وحكى مقاتل: إن الآية نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة، وأبي سفيان، وأبي جهل، وعتبة، وشيبة بن أبي ربيعة من قريش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p366/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p366/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p366/r13.claim: The mutrafūn are people made comfortable by abundance; it made them insolent, so they chose desires and disliked the burdens of religious duties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p366/r13.anchor: والمترف: المنعم، أبطرتهم النعمة، فآثروا الشهوات، وكرهوا مشاق التكاليف

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.claim: The surah challenges the worldview of the Makkan idolaters, answering their objections and addressing forms of disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.anchor: The first half of the sūrah responds to different objections that the Makkan idolaters are reported to have posed to the message of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r13.claim: A major theme is the mistaken use of ancestral tradition as a measure of truth.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r13.anchor: claiming to follow the tradition of one’s forefathers (vv. 22–25)

NAHHAS:v4p105/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p105/r1.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v4p105/r1.claim: Qatada, through Maʿmar, explains the town's mutrafū as its leaders and notables.
NAHHAS:v4p105/r1.anchor: وروى معمر عن قتادة ( إلا قال مترفوها ) قال رءوسهم وأشرافهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r1.claim: The opponents spoke to Muhammad as their predecessors had spoken to earlier messengers.
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r1.anchor: أي قد قال لك هؤلاء كما قال أمثالهم للرسل من قبلك

ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r2.claim: مقتدون means that they imitate and follow their forebears.
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r2.anchor: معناه نقتدي بهم، ويصلح أن يكون خبرا لإنا مهتدون،

ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r3.claim: على can attach to مهتدون or مقتدون, giving “guided/following in their footsteps.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r3.anchor: و (على) من صلة مهتدين، وكذلك مقتدون،

ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r4.claim: Alternatively, وإنا على آثارهم is one predicate, with مهتدون or مقتدون as a second predicate.
ZAJJAJ:v4p408/r4.anchor: ويصلح أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر، فيكون (وإنا على آثارهم) الخبر

ASAD-NOTES:43:23#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:23#n22/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:23#n22/r1.claim: Asad refers readers to note 147 on 11:116 for his rendering of mutraf, derived from tarafa.
ASAD-NOTES:43:23#n22/r1.anchor: For this rendering of the term mutraf (derived from the verb tarafa), see note 147 on 11:116.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p195#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p195#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p195#3/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the affluent leaders as the community's chiefs and notables.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p195#3/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إلا قال مترفوها ﴾ قال مترفوها رؤوسهم وأشرافهم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r1.claim: ‘Likewise’ continues the preceding point about disbelievers’ inability to argue and their retreat to imitation; inherited blind following is an old error.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r1.anchor: أي والأمر كما ذكر من عجزهم عن الحجة مطلقا وتشبثهم بذيل التقليد

ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r2.claim: The verse resumes to explain that earlier generations also had no considered proof from their own predecessors.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r2.anchor: استئناف مبين لذلك دال على أن التقليد فيما بينهم ضلال قديم لأسلافهم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r3.claim: The affluent are singled out because luxury and love of idleness diverted them from examining inherited beliefs.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p75#2/r3.anchor: وتخصيص المترفين بتلك المقالة للإيذان بأن التنعم وحب البطالة صرفهم عن النظر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p210/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p210/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p210/r3.claim: The mutrafun are a town's wealthy people and leaders.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p210/r3.anchor: {وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها} أغنياؤها ورؤساؤها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p210/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p210/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p210/r4.claim: In every town, its affluent leaders invoked their forefathers' religion and claimed to follow their example.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p210/r4.anchor: {إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون} بهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:22-24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:22-24/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:22-24/r3.claim: The recurring pattern consoles the Messenger and shows blind imitation to be an old error; earlier leaders also lacked considered evidence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:22-24/r3.anchor: تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ودلالة على أن التقليد

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:22-24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:22-24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:22-24/r4.claim: Mentioning the affluent signals that luxury and idleness distracted them from reflection and led to imitation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:22-24/r4.anchor: وتخصيص المترفين إشعار بأن التنعم وحب البطالة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r6.claim: The author consoles Muhammad by connecting Quraysh’s resistance with the same ugly conduct by earlier peoples toward their brother prophets.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r6.anchor: ومثل هذا الفعل المتناهي في البشاعة فعلت الأمم الماضية مع إخوانك الأنبياء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r7.claim: Because Muhammad is the final prophet and has no later prophet’s community as a comparison, he is consoled with past examples; nearby earlier examples console most strongly, and مِن قبلك specifies the historical scope.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r7.anchor: وقدم ذكر القبلية اهتماما بالتسلية وتخليصا لها من أن يتوهم أنه يكون معه في زمانه أو بعده نذير

BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r8.claim: The author says village inhabitants are closer to reason and sound judgment; the emphatic negation locates the point of resistance in warnings that challenge people’s desires.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r8.anchor: ولما كان أهل القرى أقرب إلى العقل وأولى بالحكمة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r9.claim: The affluent elite, indulged in fine food and ease, tend toward idleness, imitation, desire, oppression, stubbornness, and arrogance; most people commonly follow them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r9.anchor: أي أهل الترفه بالضم وهي النعمة والطعام الطيب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r10.claim: مقتدون means taking one’s model from the fathers, following and adhering to their path; the author reads the elites’ claim as rigid imitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r10.anchor: أي مستنون أي راكبون سنن طريقهم لازمون له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r11.claim: The author contrasts this wording with the parallel passage in Saba: it omits مِن قبلك there to generalize, since Quraysh had not been mentioned beforehand.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p18/r11.anchor: وأسقط هذه القبلية في ( سبأ ) لأن المراد فيها التعميم

DURR-FULL:v7p371/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the forefathers' umma as their religion.
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله

DURR-FULL:v7p371/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās tells Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq that umma means another creed, citing al-Nābigha's line as usage.
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل: {إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة} قال: على ملة غير الملة التي تدعونا إليها

DURR-FULL:v7p371/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r10.speaker: النابغة الذبياني
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r10.claim: Al-Nābigha's line is cited to show umma can mean a creed or community.
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r10.anchor: أما سمعت نابغة بني ذبيان وهو يعتذر إلى النعمان بن المنذر ويقول: حلفت فلم أترك لنفسك ريبة وهل يأثمن ذو أمة

DURR-FULL:v7p371/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r11.claim: Qatāda says Quraysh polytheists claimed they found their forefathers following a religion and would follow them.
DURR-FULL:v7p371/r11.anchor: عن قتادة {بل قالوا إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون}

DURR-FULL:v7p372/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p372/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p372/r1.claim: Mujāhid glosses following the forefathers' tracks as following their deeds.
DURR-FULL:v7p372/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون} قال: بفعلهم

DURR-FULL:v7p372/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p372/r2.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v7p372/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim says umma means a period in 12:45, a group in 28:23, and religion here; he notes the alif is raised in all cases.
DURR-FULL:v7p372/r2.anchor: عن عاصم رضي الله عنه قال: الأمة في القرآن على وجوه (واذكر بعد أمة) (يوسف الآية 45) قال: بعد حين (ووجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون)

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r4.claim: The parenthetical comparison consoles the Prophet about Meccans clinging to ancestral religion: elites in earlier towns made the same claim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r4.anchor: جملة معترضة لتسلية النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على تمسك المشركين بدين آبائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r5.claim: The opening waw either coordinates or marks parenthesis; even an interrupting waw is formally coordinated to the preceding sentence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r5.anchor: والواو للعطف أو للاعتراض وما الواو الاعتراضية في الحقيقة إلا تعطف الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r6.claim: Earlier and later peoples share this mistaken outlook through transgression; the pattern consoles the Messenger because earlier prophets faced it too.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r6.anchor: هذه شنشنة أهل الضلال من السابقين واللاحقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r7.claim: The comparison particle precedes قال مترفوها to emphasize the likeness and build anticipation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r7.anchor: وكاف التشبيه متعلق بقوله : { قال مترفوها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r8.claim: The exception clause is circumstantial: no town received a warner except in the circumstance that its elites made this claim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r8.anchor: وجملة { إلا قال مترفوها } في موضع الحال لأن الاستثناء هنا من أحوال مقدرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r9.claim: مترف is someone granted luxury and abundance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r9.anchor: والمترفون : جمع المترف وهو الذي أعطي الترف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r10.claim: Like Quraysh, the elites were intoxicated by luxury, taking God's bounty for granted and forgetting their dependence on Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p187/r10.anchor: في الازدهاء بالنعمة التي هم فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p189/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p189/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p189/r2.claim: The earlier peoples' words are paraphrased: their various statements all amount to following their fathers, a common Qur'anic and Arabic way of recounting speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p189/r2.anchor: فحكاية أقوالهم من قبيل حكاية القول بالمعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p50/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p50/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p50/r9.claim: God consoles Muhammad by showing that earlier messengers faced the same objection from their peoples' wealthy leaders.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p50/r9.anchor: ثم ضرب تعالى المثل لنبيه محمد عليه السلام وجعل له الإسوة فيمن مضى من النذر والرسل،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p308#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p308#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p308#3/r1.claim: Like the Meccans, affluent people in earlier towns claimed to follow their forebears' tradition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p308#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ وكذلك ﴾ أي وكما قالوا قال مترفو القرى من قبلهم ﴿ وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون ﴾ بهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p224/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p224/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p224/r3.claim: Earlier nations who rejected messengers made the same ancestral-tradition argument; their hearts resembled one another, as another passage observes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p224/r3.anchor: قد سبقهم إليها أشباههم ونظراؤهم من الأمم السالفة المكذبة للرسل، تشابهت قلوبهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p224/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p224/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p224/r4.claim: In every town where a warner came before Muhammad, its affluent leaders answered that they found their fathers following a religion and would follow their footsteps.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p224/r4.anchor: إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون

BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r1.claim: The ancestral argument reflects inability to produce proof and resort to imitation; inherited taqlid is an old error with no independent foundation among forebears.
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r1.anchor: أي : والأمر كما ذكر من عجزهم عن الحجة وتشبثهم بذيل التقليد.

BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r2.claim: The messengers were warners of God's punishment, and a town's mutrafun were its tyrannical, affluent leaders.
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r2.anchor: {من نذير} نبي منذر قوم من عذاب الله. {إلا قال مترفوها} : جبابرتها

BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r3.claim: Umma means a religious way or practice; muqtadun means following predecessors' customs and works.

BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r4.claim: The clause about earlier warners resumes the account and shows blind imitation long predates Quraysh.
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r4.anchor: استئناف دال على أن التقليد فيما بينهم ضلال قديم ليس لأسلافهم أيضا سند غيره

BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r5.claim: Affluent people are singled out because luxury and idleness divert them from reflection and foster imitation; prosperity can make a person insolent.
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r5.anchor: هو الذي صرفهم عن النظر إلى التقليد

BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r6.claim: The term includes rich and powerful people spoiled by abundance and distracted from the afterlife, and anyone indulging desires while recoiling from religious duties.
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r6.anchor: والمراد بالمترفين : الأغنياء والرؤساء الذين أبطرتهم النعمة وسعة العيش في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r7.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r7.claim: A hadith condemns honoring the affluent while slighting worshippers, following the Quran only when convenient, and striving for decreed gains instead of earned reward and lasting good works.
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ما بال أقوام يشرفون المترفين ، ويستخفون بالعابدين يعملون بالقرآن ما وافق أهواءهم

BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r8.speaker: قال بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r8.claim: An aphorism says God guaranteed worldly life but asked people to seek the afterlife; the wise should follow the guided and build the next life like people of certainty.
BURSEVI:v8p277#3/r8.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن الله تعالى ضمن لنا الدنيا وطلب منا الآخرة ، فليته طلب منا الدنيا وضمن لنا الآخرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.claim: They have no revealed proof; their only argument is that they found their fathers following a way.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.anchor: لا حجة لهم يستمسكون بها إلا قولهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.claim: A variant reads imma with kasra; both forms derive from the root of intending or aiming.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.claim: Umma means a way that people intend and follow, by analogy with a destination one sets out for.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes the phrase to mean a blessing or a good condition.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.claim: The phrase upon a way, and we follow can make the following clause the predicate of inna, or link the prepositional phrase to guided.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.anchor: خبر إن . أو الظرف صلة لمهتدون

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r1.speaker: قتادة وعطية
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r1.claim: Qatāda and ʿAṭiyya say umma means religion; Qays b. al-Khaṭīm’s verse is cited as evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r1.anchor: على دين , قاله قتادة وعطية , ومنه قول قيس بن الخطيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r2.claim: Mujāhid and Qutrub take it as a creed, close to the first meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r2.anchor: على ملة وهو قريب من معنى الأول , قاله مجاهد وقطرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r3.claim: Some codices read milla, ‘creed,’ instead of umma.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r3.anchor: وفي بعض المصاحف . { قالوا إنا وجدنا ءاباءنا على ملة }

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r4.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reports the meaning ‘direction of prayer.’
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r4.anchor: على قبلة , حكي ذلك عن الفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r5.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash says it means uprightness and cites al-Nābigha.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r5.anchor: على استقامة , قاله الأخفش , وأنشد النابغة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r6.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r6.claim: ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz reads the initial hamza with kasra and takes umma as a path, from ammamt al-qawm.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r6.anchor: وكان يقرأ { على أمة } بكسر الألف والأمة الطريقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r7.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r7.claim: ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz is reported to read umma with kasra on its initial hamza.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r7.anchor: وكان يقرأ { على أمة } بكسر الألف والأمة الطريقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r8.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r8.claim: Qatāda explains ‘following their traces’ as following them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r8.anchor: قال قتادة متبعون . وحكى مقاتل أن هذه الآية

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r9.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r9.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, Abū Sufyān, Abū Jahl, and ʿUtba and Shayba b. Rabīʿa.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p220/r9.anchor: أن هذه الآية نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة , وأبي سفيان , وأبي جهل

MUJAHID:v2p581/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p581/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p581/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses umma here as a religious way or community.
MUJAHID:v2p581/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ أي على ملة

MUJAHID:v2p581/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p581/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p581/r2.claim: Mujahid explains following their forebears' tracks as imitating their actions.
MUJAHID:v2p581/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ أي على ملة ﴿ وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون ﴾ أي نقتدي بفعلهم

MUQATIL:43:21-23/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:21-23/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:21-23/r4.claim: The prosperous among earlier peoples who made this claim were tyrants and leading figures.

MUQATIL:43:21-23/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:21-23/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:21-23/r5.claim: Earlier communities imitated their ancestors’ deeds just as Meccan unbelievers did.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير ﴾ نبي ﴿ إلا قال مترفوها ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r2.claim: The mutrafūn are the people pampered by prosperity, which made them arrogant: they love only desires and amusements and dislike religious hardship and duties.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r2.anchor: اى متنعموها وهم الذين اترفتهم النعمة اى ابطرتهم فلا يحبون الا الشهوات والملاهي ويعافون مشاق الدين وتكاليفه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r3.claim: This consoles the Prophet and shows that blind imitation of forebears is an old affliction.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p112#3/r3.anchor: وهذا تسلية للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وبيان ان تقليد الاباء داء قديم

QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r9.claim: The parallel wording مقتدون means followers; the other phrase means that they follow their ancestors' example.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r9.anchor: وفي الآية الأخرى «مقتدون» أي نقتدي بهم، والمعنى واحد. قال قتادة: مقتدون متبعون

QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r10.claim: The verse condemns blind imitation and thus supports rejecting it: the polytheists copied their fathers instead of considering the Messenger's call.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r10.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على إبطال التقليد لذمه إياهم على تقليد آبائهم وتركهم النظر فيما دعاهم إليه الرسول

QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r11.claim: The affluent referred to here are rulers and tyrants.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r11.anchor: والمترف: المنعم والمراد هنا الملوك والجبابرة

QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r12.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r12.claim: Muqatil says this verse was revealed about Quraysh leaders al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, and Utba and Shayba ibn Rabi'a; it consoles the Prophet because earlier peoples said the same, as 41:43 does.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:22-23/r12.anchor: وحكى مقاتل أن هذه الآية نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة وأبي سفيان وأبي جهل وعتبة وشيبة ابني ربيعة من قريش

RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r1.claim: Rāzī says worldly luxury corrupts the affluent and makes them prefer sensual pleasures and amusement while avoiding the effort of seeking truth.
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r1.anchor: والمترفون هم الذين أترفتهم النعمة أي أبطرتهم فلا يحبون إلا الشهوات والملاهي ويبغضون تحمل المشاق في طلب الحق

RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r2.claim: Rāzī quotes the Prophet that love of worldly life is the root of every sin.
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r2.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ( حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة )

RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r3.claim: Rāzī generalizes that love of this world and bodily pleasures underlies every evil, while love of God and the afterlife underlies every good.
RAZI-FULL:v27p177#2/r3.anchor: رأسي جميع الآفات حب الدينا واللذات الجسمانية ورأس جميع الخيرات هو حب الله والدار الآخرة

STUDYQURAN:43:23/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r1.claim: Leaders and notables usually resist messengers most because they benefit from a corrupt social order and stand to lose most from a just one; elsewhere they are called the guilty.
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r1.anchor: the leaders or notables of a community who are usually most adamant in opposing God’s messengers, implying that they benefit from a corrupt social order

STUDYQURAN:43:23/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r2.claim: The commentary cites leaders' opposition to Moses, Noah, other prophets, and Muhammad across multiple passages.
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r2.anchor: It is the leaders and notables who are said to have opposed Moses

STUDYQURAN:43:23/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r3.claim: The disbelievers treat following their forefathers as sufficient justification for their beliefs and actions.
STUDYQURAN:43:23/r3.anchor: implies that they see following the ways of their forefathers as sufficient justification for their beliefs and actions

TAB-FULL:v20p572#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p572#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p572#2/r1.claim: As Meccan polytheists did, earlier disbelievers rejected warners sent to their towns; the prosperous leaders and elites answered that they followed their fathers’ religion and example.
TAB-FULL:v20p572#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {إلا قال مترفوها} [الزخرف: 23] قال: «رؤساؤهم وأشرافهم»

TAB-FULL:v20p572#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p572#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p572#2/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the mutrafūn as leaders, nobles, and heads of idolatry.
TAB-FULL:v20p572#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {إلا قال مترفوها} [الزخرف: 23] قال: «رؤساؤهم وأشرافهم»

TAB-FULL:v20p573/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r1.claim: The fathers’ umma means their religious community, creed, or religion.
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون} [الزخرف: 23] «قال بفعلهم»

TAB-FULL:v20p573/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r2.claim: Following their traces means following the fathers’ method and way, imitating their actions and worshipping what they worshipped.
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون} [الزخرف: 23] «قال بفعلهم»

TAB-FULL:v20p573/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r3.claim: Muhammad’s polytheist opponents merely follow earlier idolaters in rejecting his counsel and using inherited custom to justify remaining in false religion.
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون} [الزخرف: 23] «قال بفعلهم»

TAB-FULL:v20p573/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r4.claim: Mujāhid explains that they were following their fathers’ deeds.
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون} [الزخرف: 23] «قال بفعلهم»

TAB-FULL:v20p573/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r5.claim: Qatāda says they followed their fathers in this practice.
TAB-FULL:v20p573/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون} [الزخرف: 23] «فاتبعوهم على ذلك»

TABATABAI:43:20-23/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:20-23/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:20-23/r11.claim: Ancestral imitation also marked earlier polytheist communities: their affluent leaders answered each warner by citing their forefathers’ religion and refusing to abandon it.
TABATABAI:43:20-23/r11.anchor: أي إن التشبث بذيل التقليد ليس مما يختص بهؤلاء

TABRISI:43:21-25/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:21-25/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وحفص والباقون وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:43:21-25/r1.claim: Ibn Amir and Hafs read “he said,” the rest “say”; Abu Ja'far reads “we brought you,” while the rest have “I brought you.”
TABRISI:43:21-25/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وحفص قال أولو وقرأ الباقون قل أولو وقرأ أبو جعفر جئناكم والباقون جئتكم

TABRISI:43:21-25/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:21-25/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:43:21-25/r2.claim: With “he said,” the warner addresses them; with “say,” God instructs the warner to tell them through revelation.
TABRISI:43:21-25/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: من قرأ قال فالمعنى قال لهم النذير أولو جئتكم

TABRISI:43:21-25/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:21-25/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:21-25/r7.claim: The affluent people who preferred luxury to seeking proof—the leaders—made the ancestral-tradition argument in every town.
TABRISI:43:21-25/r7.anchor: إلا قال مترفوها } وهم المتنعمون الذين آثروا الترفه على طلب الحجة يريد الرؤساء

TABRISI:43:21-25/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:21-25/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:21-25/r8.claim: Following ancestors without proof is irrational: rival groups inherit conflicting beliefs while each thinks others wrong, so one must use rational or revealed evidence.
TABRISI:43:21-25/r8.anchor: والتقليد قبيح في العقول إذ لو كان جائزا لكان يلزم في ذلك أن يكون الحق في الشيء ونقيضه

THALABI:v8p331/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p331/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p331/r9.claim: In every town, its affluent people answered a warner as Muhammad's people did, appealing to ancestral religion; muqtadūn means following and emulating them.
THALABI:v8p331/r9.anchor: وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p397#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p397#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p397#3/r1.claim: Umma means a single religion or way of belief.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p397#3/r1.anchor: إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة} أي على دين واحد (2) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p397#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p397#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p397#4/r1.claim: Umma means a single religion or way of belief.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p397#4/r1.anchor: إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة} أي على دين واحد (3) .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r1.claim: The verse says that earlier peoples gave the same reply as the people just discussed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r1.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أن غيرهم قالوا هذا القول فقال: {وكذلك} أي وكما قالوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil identify the prosperous leaders as a town's kings, elite, and tyrants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: ملوكها وأشرافها وجابرتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq says “guided” or “following” can predicate the statement “we are,” with “on their tracks” attached to it, yielding “we follow their path.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق قوله: {مهتدون} و {مقتدون}، يصلح أن يكون جوابا ل: {إنا}، و {على} من صلته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r4.claim: Alternatively, Abu Ishaq parses “on their tracks” as one predicate of “we are,” with “guided” and “following” as further predicates.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p29/r4.anchor: ويصلح أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر، فيكون (على آثارهم) خبر (إنا) ومهتدون [خبرا ثان]

ELMALILI:43:16-25/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:16-25/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:16-25/r1.claim: Umma means a community or sect that one follows, or a nation.
ELMALILI:43:16-25/r1.anchor: Arkasına düşülecek bir cemaat veya tarikat, millet.

MAJAZ:v2p202/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p202/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p202/r6.claim: Umma here means a religious way or community, with the sense of an established, upright tradition.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:23/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:23/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:23/r1.claim: Rejecting prophets and obstructing their message is a recurring response among communities that have internalized polytheism as inherited culture; Abraham's unbelieving people are a clear example.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:23/r1.anchor: hak dinden uzaklaşmış, şirki bir kültür mirası olarak içselleştirmiş bütün topluluklar peygamberlerine karşı bu tepkiyi göstermişlerdir

BURHAN:v3p68#3/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r9.claim: وكذلك sums up the recurring stance of peoples toward messengers; Zarkashi also reports the following generalization about warners as explanatory tadhyīl.
BURHAN:v3p68#3/r9.anchor: ﴿ وكذلك ﴾ 1 تذييل أي فذلك شأن الأمم مع الرسل
